items.stem: Under DOH AO 2026-0010, a previously unvaccinated person has a superficial nonbleeding cat scratch just below the eye. Which exposure category and postexposure regimen apply, in addition to wound care?

Category II: rabies vaccine without immunoglobulin
Category I: wound care without rabies vaccine

A skin-breaking scratch is not Category I contact with intact skin.

items.stem: A U.S. HHS-funded randomized trial compares two accepted fracture treatments in children. Recruitment and funding are adequate, and the question is novel and clinically relevant. The protocol plans to enroll children without seeking parental or guardian permission, although no lawful waiver or exception applies. Which FINER criterion is most directly violated?
items.rationale: The ethical criterion requires appropriate protection of research participants. Under 45 CFR 46.408(b), covered pediatric research requires adequate provisions to solicit parental or guardian permission when permission is required. The stem excludes a lawful waiver or exception.
expl: The stated recruitment and funding support feasibility; the identified problem is participant protection.
Clinical interest does not cure omission of a required permission process.
Novelty concerns the contribution to knowledge, not whether consent protections are met.

items.stem: An endometrial biopsy is taken on day 10 of a regular 28-day cycle. Which gland pattern is expected?
items.rationale: Day 10 is ordinarily in the estrogen-driven proliferative phase, when endometrial glands are relatively straight and narrow.
expl: Atrophic glands are not expected in the normal proliferative phase of a reproductive-age patient.
Fragmentation and shedding characterize menstruation.
Coiled secretory glands characterize the progesterone-driven secretory phase after ovulation.

expl: Global aphasia severely affects language production and comprehension rather than preserving fluent output.

Broca aphasia primarily causes nonfluent language production.

Dorsal root ganglion cells are first-order neurons whose dorsal-column axons have not yet crossed.

Nitrogen does not have the rapid alveolar transfer characteristic attributed here to carbon dioxide.

items.subject: Anatomy
items.stem: Which structural feature makes the center of an adult intervertebral disc depend largely on diffusion for nutrition?
items.rationale: The center of the intervertebral disc is avascular, so glucose and oxygen must diffuse from nearby vascular beds through surrounding tissue and endplates.
expl: Fenestrations would describe exchange across existing capillaries, whereas the central disc lacks an intrinsic capillary network.
Direct central arterial supply would reduce this dependence, but the mature disc center lacks such a supply.
The disc has no nutritive epithelial lining; its cells depend on diffusion through matrix.

items.stem: In a precision functional MRI study, language-selective brain regions were identified individually in children aged 4–16 years and adults. Which developmental pattern did the study find in children as young as 4?
options: Rightward language bias, with a later shift toward the left hemisphere
Symmetric language responses, with leftward bias emerging near adolescence
Adult-like leftward language bias, with connectivity still developing
Increasing leftward bias, with connectivity already at adult levels
items.rationale: The youngest studied children showed adult-like leftward language lateralization, while response magnitude and connectivity continued developing. This establishes presence by the youngest observed age, not an exact onset or a universal age of completed cerebral development.
expl: The observed early bias favored the left hemisphere, rather than a right-to-left developmental reversal.
Leftward language bias was already observed in the youngest group; delayed emergence of asymmetry was not the reported pattern.
This reverses the reported trajectories: lateralization showed no age-related increase, whereas connectivity continued maturing.

items.stem: A patient considers a burdensome intervention with little expected benefit. Which information is most relevant to deciding whether to recommend it?

Whether the intervention is considered technologically advanced
Expected benefit, burdens, and the patient's preferences
Whether a standard protocol includes the intervention

expl: Availability does not establish that the benefit outweighs this patient's burdens.
Technological complexity does not determine proportionality.
A protocol does not replace individualized evaluation of benefits and burdens.

The good effect must be achieved through the harmful effect
The good and harmful effects need only be equal
The harmful effect is not intended as the means to the benefit

expl: Consent does not replace the doctrine's intention, means, and proportionality requirements.
The harmful effect cannot be the means used to obtain the benefit.
Traditional formulations require proportionately grave justification, not mere equality alone.

Responsibility arises only from the employer's own physical act
Responsibility requires proof the employer intended the harm

items.stem: Which conclusion about hymenal wound healing is supported by McCann and colleagues' descriptive study of prepubertal and adolescent girls?
options: All hymenal lacerations heal at a uniform rate
Every healed laceration leaves a permanent visible scar
Many injuries heal rapidly without visible residual evidence
A smooth hymenal rim excludes a previous laceration

The study documented smooth or continuous appearances after healing in many cases.

expl: The cited application turned on demonstrated supervision, not mere presence.
An inference from the nature of an event concerns res ipsa loquitur, not the stated supervisory doctrine.
Apparent agency is a distinct basis that concerns representations and reliance.

options: Permanent cessation of the organism's vital functions as a whole
Reversible suppression of outward signs of life

expl: Somatic death concerns the organism as a whole.
Reversible suppression is not irreversible cellular death.
Primary flaccidity is muscle relaxation, not the definition of cellular death.

items.subject: Legal Medicine-Ethics
items.stem: A 40-year-old at 14 weeks of pregnancy has biopsy-confirmed cervical cancer. Stage IIA is suspected, but disease extent has not been established. Before selecting a definitive treatment plan, which step best supports an informed choice?
options: Set the delivery date at term before completing the cancer staging workup
Establish disease extent with indicated MRI and review the treatment implications
Schedule radical hysterectomy on the basis of the suspected stage and parity
Begin pelvic radiotherapy on the basis of the positive biopsy and patient age
items.rationale: Treatment during pregnancy depends on cancer extent and gestational age. The National Cancer Institute recommends establishing extent with indicated imaging to support informed choices; MRI is the preferred imaging modality when indicated in pregnancy. A suspected stage does not establish one mandatory definitive treatment plan.
expl: Scheduling term delivery before staging can postpone a time-sensitive cancer decision without knowing the disease extent.
Parity and a suspected stage are insufficient to select radical hysterectomy as the definitive plan.
Biopsy establishes the diagnosis, but disease extent and pregnancy-specific counseling must inform definitive treatment selection.

items.subject: Legal Medicine-Ethics
items.stem: During an adolescent consultation in the Philippines, a 16-year-old who has decision-making capacity requests voluntary HIV testing and receives appropriate counseling. Under Republic Act No. 11166, whose consent is required for this test?
options: Written consent from the adolescent and the parent
Authorization from a court before either person can consent
The parent’s written consent in place of the adolescent’s consent
items.rationale: Section 29(a) permits a person aged 15 to below 18 years to consent to voluntary HIV testing without parental or guardian consent. The general requirement is written consent, with proper counseling. This is a specific statutory rule for this test.
expl: Parental consent is not a statutory prerequisite for voluntary HIV testing in this age group.
The stated voluntary testing circumstance does not require a court order.
For a capable 16-year-old, the statute obtains consent from the adolescent, rather than substituting parental consent.

items.subject: Legal Medicine-Ethics
items.stem: Under directive 58 of the USCCB’s 2025 Ethical and Religious Directives, which circumstance can make medically assisted nutrition and hydration morally optional?
options: Significant physical discomfort caused by complications of the means used
A prolonged need for care despite effective, tolerable nutritional support
Permanent unconsciousness despite effective, tolerable nutritional support
Loss of the ability to swallow despite effective, tolerable tube feeding
items.rationale: Within this explicitly Catholic framework, medically assisted nutrition and hydration can become morally optional when they cannot reasonably prolong life or when they are excessively burdensome or cause significant physical discomfort. The directive does not make unconsciousness, impaired swallowing, or prolonged care alone sufficient to remove the obligation.
expl: Duration of care is not the stated exception when nutrition and hydration remain beneficial and tolerable.
The directive includes patients in a chronic, potentially irreversible state within the general obligation when support can prolong life without excessive burden.
Loss of oral intake is a reason assisted nutrition may be needed, not itself the stated exception.

items.stem: In Dalal and colleagues’ 1989 study of major pelvic ring disruption, which associated injury, compounded by shock, was specifically identified as a significant contributor to death in the lateral-compression group?
items.rationale: The study reported brain injury compounded by shock as significant contributors to death in lateral-compression injuries. The reported organ-injury patterns varied by mechanism; this does not establish one universal ranking for all pelvic fractures.
expl: Liver injury was among the visceral injury patterns that increased with more severe anteroposterior compression; it is not the specified lateral-compression finding.
Bowel injury increased with anteroposterior-compression severity; it is not the specifically stated finding in the question.
Splenic injury was included in the anteroposterior-compression pattern, not the particular brain-injury and shock finding asked here.

items.subject: Legal Medicine-Ethics
items.stem: In Cruz v. People (G.R. No. 166441, October 8, 2014), which intent must direct overt acts establish to distinguish attempted rape from acts of lasciviousness?
options: Intent to perform a lewd physical act
Intent to make unwanted sexual contact
items.rationale: The Court identified intent to have carnal knowledge, established by direct overt acts, as the distinguishing feature. Sexual gratification, unwanted contact, and lewd conduct can occur in acts of lasciviousness without establishing that further intent.
expl: A lewd act is not sufficient to establish that the offender had progressed toward carnal knowledge.
Sexual gratification does not by itself distinguish attempted rape from acts of lasciviousness.
Unwanted sexual contact does not necessarily establish the specific intent to achieve carnal knowledge.

items.subject: Legal Medicine-Ethics
items.stem: Under INTERPOL’s 2023 Disaster Victim Identification Guide, which finding is a secondary identification aid under articles or evidence rather than a primary identifier?
options: A verified comparison of antemortem and postmortem DNA
A verified comparison of dental records and findings
A verified comparison of friction-ridge impressions
An engraved ring found attached to the body
items.rationale: Jewelry and other personal effects are secondary identification aids. An engraving may provide a useful clue, but the item’s association with the person must be evaluated. Friction-ridge, dental, and DNA comparisons are primary identification methods.
expl: DNA comparison is a primary identification method.
Forensic dental comparison is a primary identification method.
Friction-ridge comparison is a primary identification method.

items.subject: Legal Medicine-Ethics
items.stem: Traditional forensic terminology describes a living person whose vital functions are so depressed that routine clinical examination may fail to detect them. What is this state called?
options: Irreversible loss of all brain function
Molecular death of individual tissue cells
items.rationale: Apparent death, also called suspended animation in traditional terminology, describes profoundly depressed signs of life in a person who remains alive. It is distinct from irreversible death and must not be used as a declaration that resuscitation is futile.
expl: Somatic death refers to death of the organism, not a living person with difficult-to-detect vital functions.
Irreversible loss of brain function is not the potentially reversible state described.
Molecular death denotes death of individual cells rather than reversible depression of vital signs.

items.stem: In Cameron’s 1894 account of Wreden’s historical test for evidence of live birth, which site was examined for changes in fetal gelatinous material and the entry of air?
items.rationale: Wreden’s historical method concerned the middle ear. Cameron also described substantial variation in the timing of the changes and cautioned that their absence was not proof that live birth had not occurred. The finding cannot establish live birth by itself.
expl: Gastric contents or air are separate observations and are not the site of the named test.
The urinary bladder is not the cavity described in Wreden’s test.
Pulmonary aeration is the basis of a different historical approach, not Wreden’s middle-ear test.

items.stem: In historical forensic descriptions, which named method examines the appearance of the finger webs when the spread hand is held in front of a light?
items.rationale: The diaphanous test is the historical transillumination observation of the finger webs. Magnus’s test uses a ligature, Icard’s test uses fluorescein, and the fingernail test observes color after pressure. Anemia and carbon monoxide can affect the transillumination appearance, so this observation cannot establish death by itself.
expl: Magnus’s test applies a ligature to a finger and observes distal changes, rather than transmitting light through the webs.
Icard’s test involves fluorescein injection, rather than a light examination of the hand.
The fingernail test examines color changes following pressure and release.

items.subject: Legal Medicine-Ethics
items.stem: PhilHealth has filed an administrative or criminal action against a health care provider. Under section 38.9 of the 2019 Universal Health Care Act IRR, how does that filing affect a separate civil action by PhilHealth?
options: It does not preclude a separate civil action in the appropriate court
It bars civil action because PhilHealth has elected a different remedy
It confines monetary recovery to the administrative proceeding
It permits civil action only after a final criminal conviction
items.rationale: Section 38.9 expressly states that an administrative or criminal filing does not preclude PhilHealth from bringing a separate civil action in the appropriate court. This describes available proceedings; it does not establish civil, criminal, or administrative liability without the applicable facts and legal elements.
expl: The provision expressly rejects the idea that the prior filing itself bars a separate civil action.
The provision expressly permits resort to the appropriate court for a separate civil action.
Section 38.9 does not make a final criminal conviction a prerequisite to filing the separate action.
